title: Proof-system acceptance probability
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, let $n$, $\ell$, and $r$ be natural numbers, and let $V$ be a probabilistically checkable proof system with these parameters. For an input word $w\colon\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to A$ and a proof word $q\colon\mathrm{Fin}(\ell)\to A$, the acceptance probability of $V$ is the probability that its verifier accepts when it is given the combined input and proof word.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a probabilistically checkable proof system with parameters $A,n,\ell,r$
$w$ is an input word of length $n$ over $A$
$q$ is a proof word of length $\ell$ over $A$
